newsitem.title: POLAND: Wild zloty may cut foreign T-bill entry next week.
newsitem.headline: Wild zloty may cut foreign T-bill entry next week.

text.p: Foreign investors, strained by the central bank's forex market interventions this week, may refrain from bidding for large amounts of T-bills at next Monday's 800 million zloty primary tender, dealers said.

The National Bank of Poland repeatedly bought currencies at different levels this week, pushing the zloty down nearly two percentage points to 2.3 percent from the central parity rate -- the centre of the unit's 14-percent daily trading band.
"Foreign demand at next Monday's tender may be limited because of the increase in zloty volatility," said Rafal Petsch, emerging markets dealer at Bank of America in London.
"The NBP is likely trying to scare away foreign investors, drawn to Poland last week by good fundamentals," Petsch added.
However, other dealers said the weaker zloty may attract new waves of foreign investors next week despite large and seemingly unpredictable zloty swings.

"It is still a good moment to buy Polish T-bills and foreigners may continue to purchase treasuries despite the short-term exchange rate fluctuations," said Radoslaw Radziszewski, deputy chief dealer at PKO SA.
Some said foreigners were more concerned with the zloty's crawling peg devaluation, presently one percent per month and forecast at 9.1 percent in all of 1997, than short-term swings.

Dealers expected yields to stay basically flat at Monday's tender, with some upward potential for the benchmark 52-week T-bills, sold last with an average yield of 19.94 percent and for the 26-week bills, last at 19.73 percent. @
"Yields are likely to stabilise on Monday with a slight rise of the benchmark to around 20 percent possible," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior T-bill dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers expected the zloty to trade next week around 2.43 percent from the parity rate, but said foreign entry in Polish paper would seal the local currency's fate next week.

"If foreigners enter in large numbers again we could be in for another week of upward pressure on the zloty and, most likely, unpredictable central bank interventions," one dealer at a large Polish bank said. @

On Friday the NBP last intervened at about 2.6 percent from the central parity rate and later fixed the zloty at 2.9915 against the dollar and 1.8365 to the mark, an average of 2.19 percent from the dollar and mark parity rates.
On the money market large cash inflows near the end of next week were expected to keep a lid on one-day rates as banks close monthly required reserve positions with the central bank.
Overnight rates closed the week around 21 percent, while tomorrow/next were around 21.2 percent, against the central bank's main drainage rate of 21.64 percent for 14-days.
